messages.content: You are the librarian of an automated numerical-analysis lab. You only ever cite documents from the list you are given, by their ids in square brackets; you never add documents, dates or results from memory. Answer with JSON only.

Query: fewest nodes for a rule exact to degree 7 on the interval; orthogonal polynomials and their zeros

Candidate documents (the only ones you may cite):
1. [legendre-1785] 1785: Recherches sur l'attraction des sphéroïdes homogènes. Introduces the polynomials P_n(x) in the expansion of the potential of a spheroid: P_n is orthogonal on [-1, 1] to every polynomial of lower degree, satisfies a three-term recurrence, and has n distinct real zeros inside the interval. The zeros and the orthogonality are exactly what an optimal interpolatory quadrature rule needs, although the paper does not discuss quadrature.
2. [simpson-1743] 1743: Mathematical Dissertations on a Variety of Physical and Analytical Subjects. The parabolic rule with three equally spaced nodes and weights 1/3, 4/3, 1/3 on [-1, 1], exact for all polynomials of degree three because of the symmetry of the nodes about the midpoint.
3. [lagrange-1795] 1795: Leçons élémentaires sur les mathématiques données à l'École Normale. The interpolation formula that writes the polynomial through n nodes as a combination of n basis polynomials, each one at its node and zero at the others. Integrating the basis polynomials gives the weights of any interpolatory quadrature rule once the nodes are chosen.
4. [newton-1711] 1711: Methodus differentialis. Interpolation through equally spaced nodes and the quadrature rules it yields: integrate the interpolating polynomial through n equally spaced nodes to get the Newton-Cotes rules. A rule through n equally spaced nodes is exact to degree n-1 (n even) or n (n odd); the nodes are fixed, only the weights are chosen.
5. [cotes-1722] 1722: Harmonia mensurarum. Tables of the weights of the Newton-Cotes rules with up to eleven equally spaced nodes on an interval, and the observation that high-order rules of this kind have weights of both signs.

Choose up to 4 documents most relevant to the query, most relevant first, and give one short reason each. Then summarize in at most three sentences what these documents establish about the query, citing ids in square brackets. Reply with JSON: {"selected": [{"id": "...", "why": "..."}], "summary": "..."}
